chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me from Ibrahim from his father from Abdillah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked a man, 'Did you wake up fasting?' He replied, 'No.' He asked, 'Did you visit a sick person?' He replied, 'No.' He asked, 'Did you follow a funeral?' He replied, 'No.' He asked, 'Did you feed a poor person?' He replied, 'No.' He said, 'Return to your family and kiss them, for that is charity (sadaqah) from you towards them.'
ai.seo_question: What is considered charity (sadaqah) if one has not performed fasting, visiting the sick, or feeding the poor?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) identifies the lack of major ritual acts in a man’s day and redirects his spiritual effort toward familial intimacy, declaring that kissing one’s spouse is a form of charity (sadaqah). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual merit of marital affection, framing it not merely as a physical act but as a continuous, rewarded deed that sustains the household’s spiritual equilibrium.
